issues.description: The problem statement contains an inconsistent method name: it refers to get_total_number_of_students() (line 41) while the UML, test identifiers, and the solution use getTotalNumberOfStudents() (camelCase). This naming inconsistency in the specification can confuse students about the exact method name they must implement and may cause mismatches with automated tests or expected signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across the problem statement and examples. Change the occurrence of get_total_number_of_students() to getTotalNumberOfStudents() in the problem text (line 41) so it matches the UML, tests, and the solution implementation.

issues.description: The problem statement text uses a snake_case identifier get_total_number_of_students() (lines 40-41) while the UML, template comments, and the solution implementation use the Java-style camelCase getTotalNumberOfStudents(). This mismatch of the same conceptual method name across artifacts can confuse students about the exact method name they should implement in Java.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across artifacts by replacing the snake_case occurrence in the problem statement with the Java camelCase name: getTotalNumberOfStudents(). This aligns the textual description with the UML, template comments, and solution implementation and reduces student confusion.
